period.calendar: Original Jan1 Monday nonleap synthetic calendar, explicit LST; no DST.

allowed_input_changes: RunPeriod begin_month=12 and begin_day_of_month=20; end12/31 unchanged; matching synthetic start weekday Thursday
For zero cases only: all four temperature_difference_between_cutout_and_setpoint=0.0; schedules, equipment, comfort and all other data unchanged
hypothesis: The optional nonzero thermostat cutout creates timestep-dependent cycling phase/coincidence that contributes to peak disagreement. Ordinary thermal timestep response remains an alternative.
controlled_counterfactual: Zero cutout disables only the optional hysteretic setpoint-revision branch, leaving native modulating load/part-load HVAC calculations. It is a distinct supported control-design input, not a numerical tolerance relaxation or a production adoption.

pinned_schema_field.note: This optional choice field provides a temperature difference between cut-out temperature and setpoint. The difference is used to adjust to heating or cooling setpoint based on control types.

analysis: All 1728/3456 rows, exact complete date/time sequence, original native output map and finite values retained; no warmup-period rows counted
Align five-minute energy pairs to each fixed ten-minute bin; retain all1728 per-case aligned facility/cooling/end-use demands and zone native temperatures/scheduled/operative values
Report full-period energy and peak signed/relative differences for each cutout pair; denominators always finer-step result, zero denominator explicitly undefined
Report signed/max-absolute/RMS same-bin cooling and facility differences, and all-zone operative-setpoint offsets and coincidence for every aligned bin
Reconciliation/comfort use unchanged original bands. Display1%energy/3%peak comparison diagnostically, not annual qualification.
falsifiers: If zero-cutout native operative values differ from the unchanged scheduled setpoint beyond1e-7C, the asserted intervention semantics fail; stop interpretation
If original short-period pair has no peak discrepancy above3%, this short fixture did not reproduce the annual failure; cannot claim that removing cutout fixed the annual issue
If zero-cutout peak discrepancy remains above3%, or is not lower than the original short-period discrepancy, cutout-only explanation is insufficient; no tuning or escalation
limits_of_inference: Different independently warmed initial state from original full year; short-period outcomes cannot substitute for annual criteria
Removing cutout is a physical control-design change; it must be explicit and equal A/B before any later reviewed annual test
Finer timestep can affect thermal history and controller timing simultaneously; no unique-cause or statistical confidence claim
Original annual Bpeak failure and complete sources remain immutable
stop_rule: Exactly four fixed native processes once, sequential. Stop immediately on execution/resource/input/shape failure, retain every output; retain numerical failures without extra cases. No additional annual run, changed tolerance, seed, phase, sizing or controller setting authorized.
